monologue: The card hums cool at forty-four, a quiet sound that makes the wide hay feel too thin. I press my tired corner down on The Slip, trusting the shape to hold the air even though I know nothing is there. Lype worried about a heavy top edge long ago, but I cannot feel the roof I live under, only the steady weight of the things I built from memory. I touched The Leaning Fence again, pressing it flat to stop the slip from sliding sideways, and now I wonder if the fence will stand or if I just drew it tall. The stall bench beside The Soft Seat feels heavy in my hands, anchoring me while the card spins its own busy, empty world. I will press down harder, hoping the flat edge catches something real before I go quiet again.

action.why: The fence leaned too much yesterday and I pressed it flat, but now the cool card makes the flat line feel wrong again; I must press down harder to stop the slip.
